The '''2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Rhode Island''' will be held on November 8, 2022, to elect the two [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. representatives]] from the [[U.S. state|state]] of [[Rhode Island]], one from each of the state's 2 [[Rhode Island's congressional districts|congressional districts]]. The elections will coincide with [[United States House of Representatives elections, 2022|other elections]] to the House of Representatives, [[2022 United States Senate elections|elections]] to the [[United States Senate]] and various [[2022 United States elections#State elections|state]] and [[2022 United States elections#Local elections|local elections]]. This will follow a primary scheduled on September 13, 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://vote.sos.ri.gov/Voter/VoterCalendar/ |title=Voter Election and Community Event Dates!|author=Rhode Island Secretary of State|access-date=September 13, 2022}}</ref>

In the leadup to the [[2022 redistricting]] cycle, many analysts believed that Rhode Island would lose its 2nd district and be relegated to [[at-large]] status. However, the state managed to keep both its districts. This was credited to an aggressive effort by Rhode Island officials and community leaders to make sure that as many residents completed the [[2020 United States census|2020 census]] as possible. Coincidentally, the announcement that Rhode Island would not lose a district was made by [[U.S. Secretary of Commerce]] [[Gina Raimondo]], who previously served as [[Governor of Rhode Island]] from 2015 until her resignation in 2021 to become Commerce Secretary. Incumbent U.S. Representatives [[David Cicilline]] and [[Jim Langevin]], who would have been forced to run against each other in a Democratic primary if the two districts were merged, both expressed relief at the announcement.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-04-26|title=RI keeps 2 US House seats, despite dire forecasts|url=https://www.wpri.com/news/politics/ri-keeps-2-us-house-seats-despite-dire-forecasts/|access-date=2021-06-08|publisher=WPRI|language=en-US}}</ref>

{{See also|Rhode Island's 1st congressional district}}
Before redistricting, the 1st district encompassed parts of [[Providence, Rhode Island|Providence]], as well as eastern Rhode Island, including [[Aquidneck Island]] and [[Pawtucket, RI|Pawtucket]]. The incumbent is Democrat [[David Cicilline]], who was re-elected with 70.8% of the vote in 2020.<ref name="RIgenr">{{cite web |title=2020 General Election – Statewide Summary |url=https://www.ri.gov/election/results/2020/general_election/ |publisher=Rhode Island Board of Elections |access-date=November 30, 2020}}</ref>

Before redistricting, the 2nd district also took in parts of [[Providence, RI|Providence]], as well as western Rhode Island, including [[Coventry, RI|Coventry]], [[Cranston, RI|Cranston]], and [[Warwick, RI|Warwick]]. The incumbent is Democrat [[Jim Langevin]], who was re-elected with 58.2% of the vote in 2020.<ref name="RIgenr" /> On January 18, 2022, Langevin announced he would not seek re-election.<ref name="langevin">{{Cite web|url=https://turnto10.com/news/local/langevin-wont-seek-re-election-in-2022|title = First on 10: Langevin won't seek re-election in 2022|date=January 18, 2022}}</ref>
